title: The lost coin (Luke 15:8–10)
hookLine: a woman lights a lamp, sweeps the whole house for one coin, then throws a party

cards: Keys. They were on the counter a minute ago. Pockets, twice.
Couch cushions. Hands and knees with a phone flashlight, peering under the fridge. Then there they are, and the whole morning changes.
Right after the lost sheep, Luke tells a second story, indoors. A woman has ten silver coins, and one is gone. She lights a lamp, grabs a broom, and sweeps the whole house until she finds it.
Then she does something nobody does with found keys. She throws a party.

teach.b: The King James: "Either what woman having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a candle, and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she find it?" A drachma is a small silver coin.
Not a fortune, but not nothing to her.
She has three tools: a lamp, a broom, and patience, and she keeps going until. Why does one coin matter so much? The story doesn't say.

Some suggest her savings, or part of a family set, but that's a guess. Then the party: "she calleth her friends and her neighbours together, saying, Rejoice with me; for I have found the piece which I had lost."
The party may well have cost more than the coin, and some readers think that's the point: the joy is bigger than the thing.
Jesus ends it: "there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth." Here's the quiet surprise. Yesterday the searcher was a shepherd.
Today it's a woman sweeping her kitchen.

teach.h: THE SEARCHER HAS A WOMAN'S FACE.
teach.b: Christians often read the shepherd as a picture of God, and some readers, ancient and modern, notice that this story, told right beside it, gives the same searching love a woman's face.
Same crowd, too: people grumbling about who he ate with. His answer, twice now: when someone is found, you don't file it away. You call the neighbors.

how: Christians read the lost coin together with the lost sheep and the prodigal son, the three stories of Luke 15, as pictures of God searching for people and rejoicing when they come home.

games.why: she lights a lamp, sweeps the house and seeks "diligently till she find it." then she throws a party.

practice: Look back over the past few weeks for one small thing you found again: a lost earring, a friend you reconnected with, a habit you picked back up, a good night's sleep after a bad week.
Hold it in mind and let yourself be properly glad, the way she was. If you pray, give thanks for it; if you don't, let the gladness sit there a while.
